overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance reveals that space-related 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary phenomena (such as liquid diamond planets, dark planets, and unusual cosmic conditions) generate the highest views-per-day, likes-per-view, and engagement ratios. Content focusing on space exploration, extreme physics, and counter-intuitive cosmic comparisons vastly outperforms standard psychological facts and older historical or animal trivia in the recent 7-day window. Viewers strongly engage with visual, high-stakes hypothetical questions.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) show massive traction compared to standard biological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Allocate 70% of upcoming production capacity to high-stakes space exploration and extreme planetary survival scenarios.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring extreme celestial contrasts like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) drive high view-velocity and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Use counter-intuitive planetary physics and extreme cosmic comparisons as the core hook structure for future space shorts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) show minimal traction in recent observations.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia unless integrated into a high-stakes survival or sci-fi scenario.

weak_patterns.pattern: Redundant Animal Trivia Without Extreme Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated or simple animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (low relative engagement outside of outlier pushes) underperform compared to cosmic anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content into cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric context rather than simple encyclopedic facts.
